_schema: THE TOWN'S PEOPLE. One record per person; npc.js reads it and owns no coordinate, name or behaviour of its own. FIELDS — id: unique key. name: the E-prompt name (the dialogue window's nameplate comes from dialogue.json's speaker table, not from here). scene: a scene key or a LIST of them; a town villager lives in both the real-time explore bundle (townwalk) and the cinematic one (del-cine), which share the same world coordinates because del-cine ships the whole town's collision. position: RUNTIME [x, height, -y] — the town map authors [x, across-gorge, height], so a map pos [80.73, 16, 14] is [80.73, 14, -16] here. Every position below is a vertex of the town's own derived walk network (townmap/dellhollow.routes.json), so nobody stands off the path. facing: THE POST YAW, in degrees about +Y — 0 looks down runtime +Z (which is map -Y: the near side of the gorge, the side the fixed cameras and the shop doors are on), 90 looks down +X. Same convention play3d turns the player with. Honoured by body.type 'model' AS A POST: a wander errand turns the body with its travel and the yaw eases back here when the errand ends. IGNORED by a billboard, which always turns to the camera. height: multiple of the engine's charH (MODEL_H, the [ / ] dial), so re-tuning the player re-tunes the town; a model with no height of its own takes defaults.adultHeight, so the grown-ups are not all exactly as tall as a nineteen-year-old. body.type: 'billboard' (a chroma-keyed pose plate, today) or 'model' (a GLB, the day one exists — npc.js already loads it). body.src: the plate, page-relative. body.tint: multiplies the plate, which is how the chapter-2 expansion script dresses a REUSED villager sheet as somebody else ('reuse the poppy sheet, tint #d9b08a'); see bodyNote for who is wearing whose coat. body.plate: the chroma-key plate a person wore BEFORE they were given a body — kept, unread by npc.js, so handing a body back is an edit to body.type and body.src alone. body.h: a MODEL's height multiple where it differs from the plate's (npc.js prefers it over the record's height). idleBehavior: 'stand' | 'lean' (a few degrees into whatever they lean on) | 'wander' (a small errand on the walk network, WALKLOCK semantics: a step that leaves the network or hits a wall ends the errand). radius: talk reach in metres. dialogue: a node id in game/dialogue.json. shop: a shops.json id — marks a keeper, whose greeting node opens the counter via its own effect, so the player is greeted and THEN traded with.
_canon: Cast, placement and voice are from docs/chapter2-dellhollow-script.md, docs/chapter2-expansion-script.md and docs/VOICES.md. Odessa's post is the lockhead ('the senior lockkeeper's working post' — the town map says so); she and Maren live at the Keepers' Cottage. Hobb is nineteen days into the stopped queue; Pell keeps the wicks; Sorrel prices everything; Creel splices what the town hangs from; Nib administers the gulls. The eel-wife and the boatwright are canon ROLES the scripts name without naming (a woman selling eels, the boatwright's shed) and carry title nameplates rather than invented names. Nobody here carries a plot fact and nobody says the word 'afraid'.
_artNote: Only ten characters in public/assets/char-manifest.json ship a keyed pose plate, and five of these villagers (Hobb, Pell, Sorrel, Creel, Nib) are specified in the scripts as sprite-first, nameplate-only extras on REUSED, TINTED villager sheets. bodyNote records the loan for the art pipeline: replace src (and drop tint) the day the character is drawn, and nothing else changes. 2026-07-31: seven of them wore a rigged GLB (body.type 'model'), retargeted from the four Tripo deliveries finn/mara/maren/pip by tools/vesper_retarget.py's NPC recipe (Walk_Loop, not the player's jog); body.plate keeps the plate each of them wore, so the loan is still recorded and still reversible.
_bodies: EVERY PERSON IS A BODY (user ruling, 2026-08-01, after playing: 'swap those all out for the existing 3D models, even if we have to reuse them a bunch of times'). There is no human billboard left in either town. Four rigged GLBs carry all of them — finn (adult man), mara (adult woman), maren (young woman), pip (child) — and the variation is body.tint and body.h, which is the SAME device the expansion script already licensed for the plates ('reuse the poppy sheet, tint it'), now worn by a mesh instead of a texture. TWO BILLBOARDS SURVIVE AND BOTH ARE THE CAT: there is no quadruped model, and a human GLB squashed to 0.30 charH is a worse defect than the plate it replaced (a tiny person, not a cat). Mochi keeps his plate in both towns until a cat is delivered; that exception was ratified by the coordinator in the same pass. HEIGHT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE VARIATION: defaults.adultHeight 1.10 is the standard grown-up, and a record states its own body.h only when the person is not one — 1.13 for a tall senior, 1.05 for a stooped old man, 0.70-0.76 for the children. A street where everyone is exactly 1.10 reads as one model pasted eleven times, which is the thing this ruling was issued against.

npcs.name: Odessa
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: mara's 3D model, tinted the slate of her own nameplate (#5a7a8f) and stood at 1.13 — the tallest adult in the town, because she is the one the queue looks at. Her own art is a plate only; body.plate keeps it for the day a lockkeeper is modelled.
npcs.note: The Lockhead — her working post, overlooking Lock Five below. Canon station.

npcs.name: Maren
npcs.note: The lock apron between the moorage and Lock Five — the water end of the town, which is where she is when nobody is making her be anywhere else. Facing 120: down-gorge to Lock Five (+X), quarter-turned to the near side so the 'lockfive' shot gets her face and not her shoulder.

npcs.name: Captain Hobb
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model, tinted ochre (nameplate-only extra, per script §b)
npcs.note: Leaning on his barge-pole by the slipway, where the stopped queue is rafted up. Facing 200: down the slipway and out at the rafted queue, which is also the 'boatyard' shot's side — he was authored 20, which is dead away from both.

npcs.name: Watchman Pell
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model, tinted the same watchcoat sage the plate carried. 1.12 — a lamp-ladder man is a long one. Hobb wears the same file 27 m away in ochre at 1.10; the tint and the height are what keep them two people.
npcs.note: At the notice board, doing the noon wicks — the day shift, which is the grudge.

npcs.name: Sorrel
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: maren's 3D model, carrying the terracotta the poppy plate wore (the script names that sheet for Sorrel by name, and the tint is how the loan survives the swap to a mesh). Maren herself stands 27 m down and 13 m below at the lock apron, untinted — the only two wearers of this file in the town, and they never share a shot.
npcs.note: The Harbour Deck at the market-stall end: her bread-window, relocated to the quay the town actually built.

npcs.name: Old Creel
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model, tinted the pale the rowan plate wore, at 1.05 — the shortest adult in the town, because he is eighty and the timber outlasted his knees. leanDeg is kept though npc.js only reads it on the plate path: it is the record of the pose, and the day a model learns to lean it is already written.
npcs.note: The Weave's stilt-cluster deck — laundry lines, drying racks, rope bridges: everything that hangs.

npcs.name: Nib
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: pip's 3D model — the script asks for the smallest villager available, and he is a child at both ends of the pipeline
npcs.note: The fish dock, where the gulls are — an eight-year-old's whole civil service. Facing 160 is the POST he eases back to when an errand ends: along the dock toward the eel-stall, water and gulls in front of him.

npcs.name: Eel-wife
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: mara's 3D model, tinted cool
npcs.note: 'A woman selling eels shouted a price at them on principle' — Beat 2, verbatim. Title nameplate: the scripts never give her a name and neither do we.

npcs.name: Boatwright
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model in tar-and-timber, 42 m and a district away from Creel's loan of the same file, and 1.09 against Creel's 1.05.
npcs.note: At the pitch kettle below the boatwright's shed — tar smoke curling over the water, which is the smell of the boatyard and also his first line.

npcs.name: the cat
npcs.bodyNote: THE ONE BILLBOARD LEFT IN DELLHOLLOW, and it is deliberate (see _bodies). The 2026-08-01 ruling swapped every human plate for a GLB; the four models are all bipeds, and a human squashed to 0.30 charH is a tiny person, not a cat. He keeps the plate until a cat model exists — one field, body.type, changes that day.
npcs.note: 'Mochi has located the eel-stall. The party's marching order has quietly changed.' — Beat 2. He is at the fish dock because of course he is.

npcs.name: deckhand
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in a washed grey-green. Bust del.deckhand -> villager-man.
npcs.note: The shop street between the chandlery and the weapon shop. THE REASON: nineteen days of stopped queue is nineteen days of crews with nothing to do and money they were meant to spend downriver — the shelf street is where a bored deckhand ends up, and it is the one stretch of Dellhollow with three doors and nobody outside them. Facing 20 is up-street toward the inn, which is where he is drifting.

npcs.name: net-mender
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: mara's model in undyed hemp. Bust del.netmender -> villager-woman.
npcs.note: The Weave deck between the pilot cluster and the huts, on the drying-decks run. THE REASON: the district is named for what hangs in it and Creel splices the rope, but nothing in the shot said what the DECKS are for — she is the answer, 4.5 m from Creel's post and turned the other way (facing 300, out over the drying racks) so the two read as a working deck rather than a pair.

npcs.name: old woman on the stair
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: maren's model, greyed and stood at 1.02. Bust del.stairgran -> elder-woman.
npcs.note: The loop landing — the ONE flat step in the whole stair-street, where the shelf road turns down to the quay. THE REASON: a town of four hundred years of stairs has to show somebody who has run out of them; the landing is the only post in Dellhollow where standing still is the obvious thing to be doing. Facing 210 is down the stairs she is not going to take yet.

npcs.name: fisher
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in wet slate-teal. Bust del.quayfisher -> fisher.
npcs.note: The waterfront planking west of the fish dock, at the deep-stairs foot. THE REASON: the eel-wife SELLS river fish at the stall 10 m east and nobody in the town CATCHES any — he closes that loop, and he is the only figure on the long empty run between the boatyard and the dock. Facing 180 is out at the water, which is where a line goes.

npcs.name: girl with a stick
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: pip's model, cooled — the town's second child, and the only other body small enough to be one. Bust del.gullgirl -> child-girl.
npcs.note: The Harbour Deck outside the cookhouse door. THE REASON: 'two children ran down between the party without apology' is verbatim in the expansion script and Nib is the only child in the data — one kid is an oddity, two is a town. She is on the QUAY tier and he is on the dock 13 m below, so they are never the same shot and never read as a pair; she is also the fastest wanderer here (0.8) because that is the whole note.

npcs.name: chandler
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: maren's 3D model, tinted tallow (the plate on loan was poppy's; no chandler art exists at either end)
npcs.note: Behind the counter of the Chandlery — lamp oil, rope, pitch, cantilevered out over the gorge. All three keepers stand at the shop archetype's KEEP zone (tools/item_int_build.py: 'behind counter, y 1.3..2.5, NPC stands here'), which is what runtime z -1.55 is: they were at -1.02, INSIDE the counter carcass (its back panel is y 1.03..1.08), and from the room's own high 3/4 camera the counter top at 1.05 m then cut them off at the chin. Reach follows them back: 2.7 covers the far corner of walk_pad_counter (2.55 m), so the keeper still greets a player anywhere on his own pad.

npcs.name: weaponsmith
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model, tinted cool

npcs.name: armorer
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: mara's 3D model, tinted

npcs.name: Elder Rowan
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model in the forest green of his own overcoat, at 1.06 — he is in his seventies. Rowan has a bust, three expressions and a keyed plate of his own; the GLB is the missing half and is on the list the coordinator holds (rowan/poppy/mochi/lake).
npcs.note: The square, at the front edge of the festival dais. THE POST is docs/plans/ch1-staging-audit.md's (festival-dais, map 60.4/40.4); the 0.6 m offset is measured, not taste — lm_festival-dais_deck is x[58.5..62.3] z[-41.8..-39.0] with its top at y1.94 and NO walk mesh on it, so the audit's exact centre is a man standing on scenery the player cannot reach. z -42.4 is the plaza plate at the deck's square-facing edge: same beat, inside the talk radius, on the network. Facing 114 is at the Heartlight.

npcs.name: Poppy
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: mara's 3D model in bakery terracotta. Poppy's own GLB is outstanding (see rowan).
npcs.note: Her own doorstep — walk_pad_bakery, the door AND the serving window in the same wall, which the map calls 'warm window on the square'. The audit's post is the bakery landmark (47.2, 45.4); that is the building CENTRE and has no walk surface, so the pad 3.4 m east of it is the same post made standable. Facing 85 is out at the square, which is the direction a bread-window faces.

npcs.name: Mara
npcs.bodyNote: her own body, untinted — one of the four deliveries, and the only Emberbrook adult wearing the file it was made for.
npcs.note: The square, on the well spur. The audit's post is square-plaza (64, 44) — that is the Heartlight's own plinth (lm_heartlight_plinth x[62.85..65.15] z[-45.15..-42.85]), so this is the nearest network vertex clear of it, 2 m west. Facing 255 is at Pip, which is where she is looking.

npcs.name: Pip
npcs.bodyNote: his own body, untinted. 0.70 — he is seven, and he is the shortest person in either town.
npcs.note: The square between the well and his mother. 'Orbits Mara' is the audit's own word and wander is what it means: 2 m of orbit, and facing 75 is the POST he eases back to, which is Mara. His den at pond-lane (78.6, 50) is his other place and is 18 m away — this one is where he is on a festival evening.

npcs.name: Finn
npcs.bodyNote: his own body, untinted.
npcs.note: The pond jetty. CONTESTED POST, PARKED HERE ON PURPOSE: emberbrook.map.json lists finn under square-plaza.residents, chapter1.js posts him at the pond, and docs/plans/ch1-staging-audit.md raises the disagreement as one of the seven questions for the user — unresolved. He stands at the pond because the SCRIPT is shipped content and the map's residents line is older; his smokehouse is 7 m up the shore, which is the corroboration. Reversing this is one position line. Facing 124 is out over the water.

npcs.name: the cat
npcs.bodyNote: THE SECOND AND LAST BILLBOARD (see _bodies): there is no cat model, and a biped GLB at 0.30 charH is a tiny person. A cat is on the same outstanding-GLB list as rowan/poppy/lake.
npcs.note: The waystone, OUTSIDE the arch on the Whisperwood road — the user's 2026-08-01 REDLINE puts it there and names it as where Mochi hires himself to Vesper. A SECOND RECORD, not a move: id 'mochi' is the Dellhollow cat at the eel stall and both towns need him, so the two posts are two records with two ids and two hail nodes. Same plate, same cat.

npcs.name: the miller
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: mara's model in flour-dust. THE MILLER IS A WOMAN BECAUSE THE FRAME SAID SO: authored as finn tinted, she and emb.neighbour 8.5 m up the lane were the same model in near-identical greens, and the Home Row screenshot showed the two of them in ONE FRAME as one figure pasted twice — the exact defect _bodies warns about. A different model was the fix; tint and height alone were not enough at that distance. Bust emb.miller -> villager-woman.
npcs.note: Mill lane, at walk_pad_watermill. THE REASON: the map names this edge 'mill lane' and the watermill is the only working building on Home Row; a mill with nobody at the wheel-gate is a prop. Facing 124 is at the mill door.

npcs.name: neighbour
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in warm russet — deliberately the furthest tint from the miller's flour-grey, because these two share Home Row (see her bodyNote).
npcs.note: Home lane, the first bend below the square. THE REASON: Home Row is where the village LIVES and it is the emptiest walkable stretch in Emberbrook — five doors and, until now, nobody between them. He is walking up to the square, which is what everyone in this village is doing tonight, so he wanders rather than stands. Facing 47 is up the lane.

npcs.name: old woman at the washline
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: maren's model, greyed and stood at 1.01. Bust emb.townsfolk -> elder-woman.
npcs.note: Washline green. THE REASON is the map's own: this landmark's residents list is ['townsfolk-b'] and nothing stood behind that name — she is it. Washing comes in before dark on the last night of autumn. Facing 200 is at the lines.

npcs.name: girl in the square
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: pip's model, warmed. Bust emb.girl -> child-girl.
npcs.note: The square, between the village bell and the notice board. THE REASON: impliedScale's DENSIFICATION RULING says the square is crowded at the Kindling Hour with background villagers, named cast the interactive minority — this is the first instalment, and children are what a festival square has. She keeps 2 m clear of the bell posts (x[67.47..68.53]) at full wander.

npcs.name: boy on the pond lane
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: pip's model, cooled and a little taller than Pip. Bust emb.boy -> child-boy.
npcs.note: Pond lane, 1 m from pips-den. THE REASON: the den is Pip's and Pip is up at the square with his mother, so somebody is waiting at it — which is the only way a prop called 'Pip's den' says anything while Pip is elsewhere. Facing 200 is at the den.

npcs.name: innkeeper
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: maren's model in brick-red. Bust emb.innkeep -> innkeeper.
npcs.note: The Ember Hearth's parlour, at the OPEN END of the reception counter. Measured, not chosen: the carcass rc_top is x[0.56..2.59] z[-6.26..-5.50] and the back wall YB is at z -6.30 — 0.04 m of clearance, so there is no behind-the-counter zone in this room the way the Dellhollow shop archetype has one. x 3.45 is past the carcass end on plain floorboard — authored at 2.90, moved 0.55 m out because the first screenshot had her half behind the tub at the counter's end. Facing 90 is at the door and the tables rather than at walk_pad_counter (302, as authored): a player entering this room from walk_pad_door at x 7.2 was arriving behind her head. NO shop field: docs/plans/ch1-staging-audit.md Q1 asks the user whether the inn and the store even trade on Emberwake night, and MECHANICS.md says the festival runs on gifts BY LAW. She greets and nothing else; the day Q1 says otherwise, 'shop' is one field. TITLE NAMEPLATE, no name — the map calls her 'innkeep' and inventing a proper noun for her is the user's call, not this lane's (the inn's own name is already pending their blessing).

npcs.name: shopkeeper
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: mara's model in undyed linen. Bust emb.shopkeep -> villager-woman.
npcs.note: The Village Store, inside the L of the counter — ct_top is x[1.55..4.55] z[-3.25..-2.55] with the return at x[3.85..4.55], so z -3.80 is 0.55 m behind the top on free floorboard, which is the Emberbrook equivalent of the Dellhollow KEEP zone all three of its keepers stand in. Facing 0 is across the counter at walk_pad_counter. NO shop field, for the same Q1 reason as the innkeeper. Title nameplate: the map calls her 'shopkeep'.
